gloss: lower seat, seat of lesser honor

definitions.gloss: lower seat, seat of lesser honor
definitions.explanation: The seat position farthest from the tokonoma (decorative alcove) or closest to the door in a traditional Japanese room. The seat taken by the person of lower status or the host. Opposite of {上座|かみざ}.

examples.japanese: {新人|しんじん}は{下座|げざ}に{座|すわ}る。
examples.english: Newcomers sit in the lower seat.

examples.japanese: {下座|げざ}は{入|い}り{口|ぐち}に{近|ちか}い{席|せき}だ。
examples.english: The lower seat is the one closest to the entrance.

examples.japanese: {上座|かみざ}と{下座|げざ}のマナーを{知|し}らないと、ビジネスの{場|ば}で{恥|はじ}をかくことがある。
examples.english: If you don't know the etiquette of upper and lower seating, you may embarrass yourself in business settings.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
Seating hierarchy ({上座|かみざ}/{下座|げざ}) is an important aspect of Japanese business and social etiquette. The rules apply in meeting rooms, taxis, elevators, and restaurants. Generally, the most senior person sits at {上座|かみざ} (farthest from the door), while the most junior sits at {下座|げざ} (closest to the door).

FORMS:
{下|げ} (lower) + {座|ざ} (seat)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {下座|げざ}に{座|すわ}る: to sit in the lower seat
- {上座|かみざ}と{下座|げざ}: upper and lower seating positions
